text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server responds with data, often in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps your application respond properly when something goes wrong, such as a network failure or an invalid request.
